units.translation: Thus M, where γε μείζω [at least greater] is undoubtedly corrupted from γεμίζων [filling], as can be gathered from the scholiast's annotation τοῦ Διὸς ἐμπιπλῶντος καὶ γεμίζοντος ἄτης τὸν γόμον [of Zeus filling and loading the cargo with ruin], whence Turnebus read ἄτης [ruin] and γόμον [cargo].
filling well-prepared cauldrons with the ashes of Antenor.
having filled the cargo with at least greater ruin and much of it.
of Zeus filling and loading the cargo with ruin
a thing with which something is filled, stuffing
with entrails and the organs, a pitiable stuffing, conspicuous as they hold them.
γεμόντων [being full] is a gloss written next to φλεόντων [teeming] (corrupted in M to φλεγόντων [burning]), which Hermann deleted.
such is the boast, full of truth.
a house too full of misery.
alas, having flourished in many toils, a race.
for this grief is common to the race.
a godlike man of the golden-born race.
to wear down another race with murderous deaths.
how cruelly the deity has entered the race of the Persians.
producing, natal, ancestral, of one's birth
around the stream of Triton, the natal passage.
do you not revere the ancestral curses, child?
and he calls upon the ancestral gods of his fatherland.
so that the Argive race and your seed may be preserved.
a fiery red, very full, shaggy beard.
shaggy is the mustache and the base of the beard.
in the gathering of hair on the chin.
pluck the white hair of the chin.
you will mourn for your goat's beard, indeed.
of those who pride themselves on their race.
and fitting to their own race.
behold the bereft offspring of the eagle father.
the hare's offspring, teeming in the womb.
third in race, with ten other births.
and the fifth generation from him, with fifty children.
I was born an evil to my race and fatherland.
of the mourning race of the city.
calling upon the three-cubit-tall deity of this race.
alas, father, of you and your noble children.
the bond of the oath nobly fixed.
and you will bear dark Epaphus, named after the touch of Zeus (thus Wieseler for γεννημάτων [of the offspring]).
race, offspring, with regard to stock or family or kinship
In a broader sense it is said either of the whole race of gods or men or of one particular race of men.
race, with regard to nation or state
